## Function 1
```{r}
hand_value <- function(hand) { # function with hand as argument
  ranks <- sort(as.numeric(hand$rank)) # created column vector of all of the ranks sorted by rank
  distinct_ranks <- length(unique(hand$rank)) # counted the number of distinct ranks
  straight <- max(ranks) - min(ranks) == 4 || identical(ranks, c(2, 3, 4, 5, 14)) # T/F value if hand is straight (1 rank difference between each card) (note the included ace-low hand)
  flush <- all(hand$suit == hand$suit[1]) # T/F value if hand is flush (suits are identical)
  if (flush == TRUE) {
    if (straight == TRUE) {
      if (identical(ranks, c(10, 11, 12, 13, 14))) {
        return("Royal Flush") 
        # if hand is flush, straight, and 10-A, return royal flush
      }
      else {
        return("Straight Flush")
        # if hand is flush, straight, and not a royal flush, return straight flush
      }
    }
    else {
      return("Flush")
      # if hand is a flush but not a straight, return flush
    }
  }
  else if (distinct_ranks == 2) { # if there are only 2 types of ranks in the hand
    if (ranks[1] == ranks[4] || ranks[2] == ranks[5]) {
      return("Four of a Kind")
      # if 4 of the cards are the same rank, return 4 of a kind 
    }
    else {
      return("Full House")
      # if two distinct ranks in the hand and not 4 of a kind, return full house (must be 3 of same rank and 2 of (same) other rank)
    }
  }
  else if (straight == TRUE) {
    return("Straight")
    # if hand does not meet previous conditions and is a straight, return straight
  }
  else if (distinct_ranks == 3) { # if hand has three different types of rank
    count <- table(ranks) # count the number of cards is each rank
    if (max(count) == 3) { 
      return("Three of a Kind")
      # if hand has 3 of the same rank, return three of a kind
    }
    else {
      return("Two Pair")
      # if not three of a kind, must be 2 pair 
    }
  }
  else if (distinct_ranks == 4) {
    return("One Pair")
    # if there are 4 distinct ranks, two must be same rank, therefore return one pair
  }
  else {
    return("High Card")
    # if none of these conditions are met, return high card
  }
}
```

### test cases
```{r}
royal_flush <- data.frame( # royal flush test case
  rank = c("10", "11", "12", "13", "14"),
  suit = c("H", "H", "H", "H", "H")
)
straight_flush <- data.frame( # straight flush test case
  rank = c("5", "6", "7", "8", "9"),
  suit = c("S", "S", "S", "S", "S")
)
four_of_a_kind <- data.frame( # four of a kind test case
  rank = c("8", "8", "8", "8", "2"),
  suit = c("C", "D", "H", "S", "H")
)
full_house <- data.frame( # full house test case
  rank = c("12", "12", "12", "4", "4"),
  suit = c("C", "D", "H", "S", "C")
)
flush <- data.frame( # flush test case
  rank = c("2", "5", "9", "11", "14"),
  suit = c("D", "D", "D", "D", "D")
)
straight <- data.frame( # straight test case
  rank = c("4", "5", "6", "7", "8"),
  suit = c("H", "C", "S", "D", "H")
)
straight_ace_low <- data.frame( # straight where ace is low
  rank = c("14", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
  suit = c("H", "C", "S", "D", "H")
)
three_kind <- data.frame( # three of a kind test case
  rank = c("7", "7", "7", "2", "4"),
  suit = c("H", "C", "S", "D", "H")
)
two_pair <- data.frame( # two pair test case
  rank = c("11", "11", "5", "5", "14"),
  suit = c("H", "C", "S", "D", "H")
)
one_pair <- data.frame( # one pair test case
  rank = c("10", "10", "3", "5", "9"),
  suit = c("H", "C", "S", "D", "H")
)
high_card <- data.frame( # high card test case
  rank = c("14", "11", "8", "4", "2"),
  suit = c("H", "C", "S", "D", "C")
)
test_cases <- list(
  Royal_Flush     = royal_flush,
  Straight_Flush  = straight_flush,
  Four_Kind       = four_of_a_kind,
  Full_House      = full_house,
  Flush           = flush,
  Straight    = straight,
  Straight_Ace  = straight_ace_low,
  Three_Kind      = three_kind,
  Two_Pair        = two_pair,
  One_Pair        = one_pair,
  High_Card       = high_card
)

test_results <- lapply(test_cases, hand_value)
print(test_results)

```

## Function 2
```{r}
hand_score <- function(hand) { # created function with hand as argument
  if (nrow(hand) == 5) { # if 5-card hand, return the hand with the value of hand
    return(list(hand_value(hand), hand))
  }
  else {
    hand_order <- c("High Card", "One Pair", "Two Pair", "Three of a Kind",
                  "Straight", "Flush", "Full House", "Four of a Kind",
                  "Straight Flush", "Royal Flush") # created way to order the hands 
    combs <- combn(nrow(hand), 5) # all possible combinations
    best_rank <- 0 
    best_value <- NULL
    best_subset <- NULL # initalized variables for the best rank, value, subset
    for (i in 1:ncol(combs)) { # going through all cominations
      current_subset <- hand[combs[, i], ] # found the current subset we are evaluating
      value <- as.character(hand_value(current_subset)) # found the value of the current subset
      rank <- match(value, hand_order) # found the "rank" of the value of the subset
      if (rank > best_rank) { # if this rank if better than previous, it replaces the best rank
        best_rank <- rank
        best_value <- value
        best_subset <- current_subset
      }
    }
    return(list(best_value, best_subset)) # return best rank
  }
}
```

### test cases
```{r}
royal_7 <- data.frame(
  rank = c(10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 2, 3), 
  suit = c("H", "H", "H", "H", "H", "C", "D")  
)
fullhouse_6 <- data.frame(
  rank = c(12, 12, 12, 4, 4, 7),  # Three 12s (Queens), Two 4s, one extra 7
  suit = c("C", "D", "H", "S", "C", "S")
)
flush_7 <- data.frame(
  rank = c(2, 5, 9, 11, 14, 7, 7),  # 2, 5, 9, 11, 14 of Diamonds (a Flush) + two 7s
  suit = c("D", "D", "D", "D", "D", "H", "C")
)
test_cases <- list(
  royal_7, 
  fullhouse_6,
  flush_7
)
test_results <- lapply(test_cases, hand_score) # applying function to all of test cases
print(test_results) 
```
## Hand Simulations

### Draw Function
```{r}
# draw function from earlier r script
draw <- function(deck, n) { 
  hand <- deck |>  
    slice_sample(n=n) 
  remaining_deck <- deck |> 
    anti_join(hand) 
  return(hand) 
}
# creating deck dataframe
hearts <- data.frame(
  rank = 2:14,
  suit = "heart" 
) # created hearts df
clubs <- data.frame(
  rank = 2:14,
  suit = "club" 
) # clubs df
spades <- data.frame(
  rank = 2:14,
  suit = "spade" 
) # spades df
diamonds <- data.frame(
  rank = 2:14,
  suit = "diamond" 
) # diamonds
deck <- rbind(hearts, clubs, spades, diamonds) 
```

### 5 cards
```{r, message=FALSE}
set.seed(123)
values_5card <- data.frame( 
  value = character()
) # empty dataframe for all observations
for (i in 1:5000){ # simulate 5000 times
  hand <- draw(deck, 5) # draw 5 cards
  value <- hand_value(hand) # find value of the hand drawn
  values_5card <- rbind(values_5card, data.frame(value = value)) # add value to empty df
}
```

```{r}
all_hands <- c("High Card", "One Pair", "Two Pair", "Three of a Kind", "Straight", "Flush", "Full House", "Four of a Kind", "Straight Flush", "Royal Flush") # df of all hand types (so they all appear on graph)
values_5card |> 
  count(value) |> # create variable with count of all the hand values
  complete(value = all_hands, fill = list(n = 0)) |> # add hands that didn't appear
  ggplot() + # plot on bar chart 
  geom_col(aes(x=reorder(value, -n), y=n),  position = "dodge") +
  labs( # adding labels 
    title = 'Count of Hand Value for 5 Card Draw',
    x = 'Hand Type',
    y = 'Count',
  ) +
  theme_classic() + # adjusting axes
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

### 6 cards
```{r, message = FALSE}
# repeat sample process fo 6 cards
set.seed(123)
values_6card <- data.frame(
  value = character()
)
for (i in 1:5000){

  value <- hand_score(hand)[[1]]
  values_6card <- rbind(values_6card, data.frame(value = value))
}
```
